Biologically, maintaining cardiovascular health, metabolic balance, and adequate nutrition helps preserve function and reduce the risk of chronic disease. Psychologically, cognitive stimulation, stress management, and maintaining a sense of purpose are important for resilience and mental well‑being. Tobacco control (taxation, smoke‑free laws, cessation support), promotion of healthy diet (reducing salt, sugar, and trans‑fats; improving access to fruits and vegetables), and increasing physical activity (urban design, active transport, community programs) are central components. Screening and early detection programs for conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and some cancers enable earlier, more effective intervention. Policies addressing social determinants of health—such as education, income, housing, and access to care—are essential because they shape exposure to risk and capacity to adopt healthier behaviors. Multisector collaboration (health, education, transport, urban planning, and industry) is required to create environments that make healthy choices easier and more equitable.
